cards.explanation: The instruction is to test the spirits to see if they're from God. The writer says, "…do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God." (1 John 4:1) He doesn't tell his readers to panic or to swallow everything whole. He tells them to check. A good baker checks the dough before it goes in the oven, and a good listener checks what he hears.

The answer is PROPHETS, friends! The writer says, "For many false prophets have gone out into the world." (1 John 4:1) That's his reason for the testing. With that many voices out there, I'd check every one before it got anywhere near my ovens.

The answer is that He has come in the flesh. The writer says, "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God…" (1 John 4:2) So the thing to listen for is what a spirit says about Jesus. Confessing that He came in the flesh marks a spirit as from God.

The answer is True. The writer says, "…every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God." (1 John 4:3) It comes right after verse 2, where he says, "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God…" (1 John 4:2) Read the two verses together and you've got both sides of his test.

The answer is that it's already here, back when he wrote it. The writer says it's the spirit of the antichrist, "…which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time." (1 John 4:3) His readers had heard it was coming. He tells them it was already in the world at that time.

The answer is that someone greater is in them than in the world. The writer says, "…greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." (1 John 4:4) The overcoming isn't about how clever or how many they are. It's about who is in them, and He is greater.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, "They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them." (1 John 4:5) The world does listen to them. It's not that the world won't.

The answer is True. The writer says, "We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us…" (1 John 4:6) Knowing God and listening to his side go together in this verse. The verse also says, "whoever is not from God does not listen to us."
